L-02 · How should a roster measure the room beside the panel?

Your answer to the design review's question 1 stays as it is (v1.053, "A: room beside panel"): a roster picks its layout from the room beside the left panel, not from the window. This question is only about how the app measures that room. The design review's plan uses a CSS container query: a style rule that asks the width of a box on the page instead of the window's. The page area becomes that box, and each roster's styles ask its width. Testing it, I found a catch.

What I found: on older iPads, the container would move pop-up lists

Browsers changed how a container works: Chrome and Edge 129 (September 2024) and Safari 18.4 (iPadOS 18.4, March 2025). Before that, a container also made every pop-up list inside it measure from the container's corner instead of the window's.

The page area starts 72 px right of the window's edge (the panel) and 48 px down (the top bar). So on an older device, every list drawn inside a page would open 72 px right and 48 px down of its cell.

Today's Chrome has the new rule, so I copied the old one into it. Here it is on Star's Grading page at 820 × 1180 (an iPad held upright): Noah Chen's grade list, with the cell it belongs to outlined. It now sits under Breaking, a row lower.

The same goes for Black Belt's grade list and measured-number box, and the "kept" notes in Star and Black Belt: the grading pages used at the mat. Dialogs and ⋯ menus aren't affected: they're drawn outside the page.

Two ways to build it

A · The container query, switched on only where it's safe

When the app starts, it tests the browser with a hidden box (it takes a few milliseconds). Where pop-ups stay put, the page area becomes a container, and rosters follow the room. Elsewhere nothing changes: rosters keep today's window rules.

  • + It's the plan the sections already have: their styles ask the page area's width.
  • + A style can follow the room by itself, without the roster's code.
  • − On an iPad not on iPadOS 18.4 or newer, L-02 isn't fixed. Camps on a 768 px iPad with Largest still hides Friday (question 1's picture 3, right).
  • − Each roster writes its rules twice: the window rules stay for older devices, and the room rules are added.
  • − The school's iPads need checking (Settings → General → About).
B · No container query: the shared code measures the room (my pick)

Dashboard core's shared part measures the page area with a ResizeObserver (the browser tells the code when a box changes size; the app already uses one for the bars under the top bar). It tells each roster whether the room is narrower than that roster's own limit. The roster then draws its phone layout and puts a class on it, and its styles follow the class. The three rosters mostly work this way already: Color Belt's and Star's phone rows have the class is-phone, and Camps' cards have their own.

  • + It works on every device the app already runs on. Nothing to check, and older iPads get the fix too.
  • + Each roster's limit is written once, so its code and styles can't disagree.
  • + No pop-up can move.
  • − The three sections' fix files say @container page. Main tells them to use the class instead (one line each).
  • − A style can't follow the room by itself: it goes through the roster's code. That's the same code that already draws its phone rows.

Either way: on up-to-date iPads and PCs, A and B look the same (question 1's pictures 4–6). The four review sizes look as today (pictures 9–12), and dialogs and ⋯ menus keep following the window. The Camps pictures in A and B are the design review's (question 1's pictures 6 and 3). The Star pictures are real preview screens; the second has the old rule copied in.
